stories.new_fact: A federal appeals court upheld a block on President Trump's mail-voting executive order while the Supreme Court considers the dispute.
stories.new_takeaway: The story is now an election-operations deadline, because ballot mailing, envelope design, voter files and voter instructions cannot wait for abstract legal clarity.
stories.why_now: The appeals ruling came Thursday and AP reported it as states had already begun sending mail ballots.
stories.previous_coverage: Not covered in the previous seven episodes; recent national segments focused on Iran, labor data and inflation.
stories.uncertainty: The Supreme Court could leave the block in place, narrow the dispute, or allow parts of the order to proceed on an emergency basis.
stories.watch: Watch whether the Supreme Court acts before additional states send mail ballots.

stories.new_fact: The Italian Village Commission approved a 428-unit apartment project at 274 E. First Ave. with five buildings, a garage and demolition of the former State Library/Ohioana building.
stories.new_takeaway: Columbus housing supply depends on turning abstract growth targets into review-board approvals, financing, demolition permits and phased construction.
stories.why_now: The approval was reported September 11, with groundbreaking tentatively targeted for early 2027.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent Columbus coverage handled referendums, cameras, schools, transit and data centers; this is a fresh housing-supply approval.
stories.uncertainty: Permits, demolition timing, financing costs and neighborhood reaction can still affect when the first phase starts.
stories.watch: Watch demolition and permit filings for the 274 E. First Ave. site.

stories.new_fact: Freddie Mac says all sellers may now use VantageScore 4.0 when originating and selling eligible loans to Freddie Mac, effective immediately.
stories.new_takeaway: The operating burden moves from a Fannie Mae DU-only implementation to cross-enterprise score-model consistency across LPA, pricing, delivery and QC.
stories.why_now: The Freddie Mac implementation detail was a specific watch from Friday's episode and is a specialist update from the last seven days.
stories.previous_coverage: Friday covered Fannie Mae's DU, reporting and delivery specifics; this is the Freddie Mac side and does not repeat the same takeaway.
stories.uncertainty: Lender overlays, product exclusions, vendor readiness and delivery edits will determine how fast ordinary production use starts.
stories.watch: Watch for lender overlays, Freddie delivery cautions and early production guidance.
stories.date_exception: Quiet Saturday specialist beat: explicitly dated September 9 update changes a current lender workflow and follows Friday's Fannie watch item.

stories.new_fact: FIS said its Financial Crimes AI Agent, developed with Anthropic, is currently in pilot with core banking clients and cited Policy Optimizer 2.0 for AI-driven credit-policy analysis.
stories.new_takeaway: Financial-crimes and credit-policy agents require auditable action paths before banks can treat vendor pilots as production control improvements.
stories.why_now: The FIS release is dated September 10 and creates a new pilot row in the bank-AI deployment ledger.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent bank-AI sections covered Truist contact centers, OpenAI financial services, JPMorganChase productivity and Better mortgage AI; this is a different vendor and financial-crimes lane.
stories.uncertainty: No named bank result, fraud-loss reduction, alert-quality metric, investigation-time metric or credit-policy outcome was disclosed.
stories.watch: Watch for a named bank pilot result, independent control review or regulator-facing audit description.
stories.ledger_row_changed: FIS / Anthropic - lanes 2 and 3 - new pilot row for Financial Crimes AI Agent and Policy Optimizer 2.0 with vendor-claim evidence and no disclosed metric.

stories.new_fact: OpenAI said GPT-Rosalind is coming out of research preview and is globally available to eligible organizations through trusted access, with published pricing effective October 5.
stories.new_takeaway: The frontier signal is a vertical-model access shift: specialized models are becoming governed enterprise services rather than only research demonstrations.
stories.why_now: The update was posted September 11 and had not been covered in the prior seven episodes.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent frontier sections covered Anthropic misuse, ChatGPT Images, OpenAI Navier-Stokes and Gemini Cyber; this is a distinct access/workflow story.
stories.uncertainty: Benchmark claims are lab-reported, eligibility is controlled, and real drug-discovery or lab-cost outcomes require independent evidence.
stories.watch: Watch GPT-Rosalind pricing on October 5 and any independent life-sciences customer evaluation.
stories.frontier_bar: Price or access shift plus new capability with lab-reported benchmark evidence for a specialized model.

stories.new_takeaway: Markets are testing whether oil relief can offset Fed pressure, while Columbus weekend plans need rain and flood caution.
stories.why_now: Markets closed Friday and the weather forecast was checked Saturday morning.
stories.uncertainty: Live market assumptions and local storm placement can change quickly.
stories.watch: Watch Monday Treasury reaction and updated Columbus radar.
